title: Finite global fan-chart covers and their Cech refinements
statement:
Let $(X,M)$ be a quasi-compact locally Noetherian fs log scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-trf-fs-log-blowup] whose geometric characteristic group completions are torsion free. A strict log morphism and a global fan chart have the meanings of [lem-trf-log-fan-chart-blowup], and etale means [def-weil-etale-morphism]. There is a finite family of quasi-compact strict etale neighborhoods $u_a:U_a\to X$ which is jointly surjective and whose members have global fan charts. Its disjoint union $U=\coprod_aU_a$ [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], with its componentwise log structure, is quasi-compact, locally Noetherian and fs, has torsion-free characteristic group completions and a global fan chart to the disjoint union of the chart fans. The induced $u:U\to X$ is a surjective strict etale morphism.

For any such cover, all finite nonempty iterated fiber products $U^{[r]}=U\times_X\cdots\times_XU$ ($r\geq1$) [def-pc-fibre-product] are quasi-compact locally Noetherian fs log schemes with torsion-free characteristic group completions and global fan charts. The projections between consecutive products are surjective strict etale. If $v:V\to X$ is another such cover, then $U\times_XV$ has the same properties and both its projections are surjective strict etale. If $f:(Y,N)\to(X,M)$ is any strict etale morphism with $Y$ quasi-compact locally Noetherian fs and with torsion-free characteristic group completions, then $W=Y\times_XU$ has these properties, is globally fan-charted, and $W\to Y$ is surjective strict etale. No surjectivity of $f$ is assumed. The assertions include the empty scheme and the empty covering family when $X$ is empty.

source.place: VIII 3.3.4(ii), 3.3.12--3.3.13 and proof of 3.3.15, pp.107--110: finite disjoint-union cover and descent reduction; Cech refinements expanded.

proof.text: Apply (i) of [lem-trf-log-fan-chart-blowup] to obtain a finite jointly surjective family of quasi-compact strict etale $U_a\to X$ with fan charts $c_a:U_a\to F_a$. Since $X$ is locally Noetherian it is quasi-separated. Thus each $u_a$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1). Etale maps are unramified and hence locally of finite type by the two cited definitions; consequently $u_a$ is of finite type. The scheme $X$ is Noetherian (locally Noetherian and quasi-compact), so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes each $U_a$ Noetherian.

source.place: VIII 3.3.4(ii), 3.3.12; finite selection in proof of 3.3.15; Stacks 01OY, 03GI, 01T6

proof.text: Form $U=\coprod_aU_a$ with the disjoint open components supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. For an etale object $T\to U$, define its log sections as the product of the log sections over $T\times_UU_a$; restrictions and structural maps are componentwise. This is a log structure since sheaf gluing and the units condition hold separately on the disjoint open components. The component fs charts and affine Noetherian open covers are also open covers of $U$, so $U$ is fs and locally Noetherian by definition. Characteristics are the component characteristics and therefore torsion free, since each $u_a$ is strict. Any open cover of $U$ has a finite subcover on each quasi-compact $U_a$; their union is finite since there are finitely many $a$. Thus $U$ is quasi-compact.

source.place: VIII proof of 3.3.15, pp.109--110, disjoint unions; componentwise log construction

proof.text: Give $F=\coprod_aF_a$ its disjoint-union topology and componentwise sharp monoid sheaf. It is a fine fan: every point has exactly its original affine fan neighborhood. The maps $c_a$ define $c:U\to F$; on each open component the characteristic comparison is the given isomorphism, hence $c^{-1}\mathcal P_F\simeq\overline M_U$. The component Zariski log structures likewise give a Zariski log structure on $U$. This is a global fan chart. The coproduct map $u$ is etale by [lem-sc-etale-coproduct-etale], is surjective because the $u_a$ jointly cover, and is strict because its characteristic map at each geometric point is the strict characteristic map on that component.

source.place: VIII 3.3.12 and proof of 3.3.15, pp.109--110; Stacks 02GJ

proof.text: Now fix any cover $u:U\to X$ of the stated kind and any strict etale $f:Y\to X$ with $Y$ satisfying the hypotheses in the last clause. Set $W=Y\times_XU$ with projections $p:W\to Y$, $q:W\to U$. The singleton-cover instance of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change] makes $p$ surjective etale, without requiring $f$ surjective. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change], $q$ is etale. Since $X$ is quasi-separated and $U$ quasi-compact, $u$ is quasi-compact. Its base change $p$ is quasi-compact, so $W$ is quasi-compact as $Y$ is. Since $p$ is etale it is locally of finite type by the cited definitions; it is therefore of finite type, and its Noetherian target $Y$ makes $W$ Noetherian.

source.place: VIII 3.3.4(ii), descent reduction in proof of 3.3.15; Stacks 02GO, 01S1, 01OY, 03GI, 01K5, 01T6

proof.text: Give $W$ the log structure $N_W$ associated to $p^{-1}N$ and its map to $\mathcal O_W$; then $p$ is strict by [def-per-strict-log-morphism]. Since $f$ and $u$ are strict, $N=f^*M$ and $M_U=u^*M$; associated inverse images compose, so $q^*M_U=(uq)^*M=(fp)^*M=p^*N=N_W$ and $q$ is strict too. If $P\to N|_V$ is an fs chart on an etale $V\to Y$, its composite $P\to N_W|_{V\times_YW}$ is a chart, because the log structure associated to $P\to\mathcal O_{V\times_YW}$ is the inverse image of the one associated to $P\to\mathcal O_V$. With step 4 this makes $(W,N_W)$ a locally Noetherian fs log scheme [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. By the characteristic form of strictness, $\overline N_{W,\bar w}\simeq\overline N_{p(\bar w)}$, whose group completion is torsion free.

source.place: VIII proof of Lemma 3.3.6, printed p.107 (strictness is stable under base change; the same chart on source and target); VI 1.1

proof.text: The target $U$ of the strict map $q$ has a Zariski log structure. The first assertion of [lem-trf-strict-log-blowup-cartesian] gives a Zariski log structure on $W$ and the canonical isomorphism $q^{-1}\overline M_U\simeq\overline M_W$. Compose $q$ with a fan chart $c:U\to F$. Then $(c q)^{-1}\mathcal P_F=q^{-1}c^{-1}\mathcal P_F\simeq q^{-1}\overline M_U\simeq\overline M_W$. Therefore $cq$ is a global fan chart by the definition. Together with the preceding two steps this proves every assertion about $Y\times_XU$ in the last clause.

source.place: VIII 3.3.8, same fan chart on a strict source, and 3.3.12

proof.text: Induct on $r\geq1$. For $r=1$, $U^{[1]}=U$ has all the required properties and its map to $X$ is surjective strict etale. If this holds for $U^{[r]}$, apply steps 4--6 with $Y=U^{[r]}$ and its structure map to obtain $U^{[r+1]}=U^{[r]}\times_XU$, its properties, and its surjective strict etale projection to $U^{[r]}$. Its structure map to $X$ is strict by composition of the pulled-back log structures and is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](2); it is surjective by composition. Any other projection omitting one factor has the same description after permuting factors by the fibre-product universal property, so it too is surjective strict etale.

source.place: VIII proof of 3.3.15, descent reduction expanded to the Cech nerve; Stacks 02GN

proof.text: For a second cover $v:V\to X$, use steps 4--6 with $Y=V$. They give every stated property of $U\times_XV$ and its surjective strict etale projection to $V$. The other projection is the base change of the surjective etale $v$, hence is surjective etale by the singleton-cover instance of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change], and is strict by step 5. If $X$ is empty choose the empty covering family and the empty fan. Every scheme mapping to $X$ is then empty; all these fibre products are empty, all pointwise and covering conditions are vacuous, and every open cover has the empty finite subcover. The constructions above therefore include the empty case.

source.place: VIII proof of 3.3.15, finite disjoint-union descent; common refinements and empty case expanded

proof_origin.place: VIII 3.3.4(ii), 3.3.5--3.3.6, 3.3.8, 3.3.12 and proof of 3.3.15, pp.107--110; Cech/refinement assembly expanded with the cited Stacks scheme permanence lemmas.
